1.w: In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greater in the kingdom of the heavens?”

2.w: And having summoned a little child, He set him in their midst

3.w: and said, “Truly I say to you⁺, if you⁺ shall not be turned and become as the little children, you⁺ shall never enter into the kingdom of the heavens.

4.w: Therefore whoever will humble himself like this little child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of the heavens.

5.w: And whoever shall receive one such little child in My name, he receives Me.

6.w: And whoever might cause to stumble one of these little ones believing in Me, it is better for him that a heavy millstone should be hung around his neck and he should be sunk in the depth of the sea.

7.w: Woe to the world because of the stumbling blocks. For [it is] a necessity that the stumbling blocks come, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes!

8.w: Now if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast [it] from you; it is better for you to enter into life crippled or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be cast into the eternal fire.

9.w: And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast [it] from you. It is better for you to enter into life one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.

10.w: See that you⁺ do not despise one of these little ones. For I say to you⁺ that their angels in the heavens always see the face of My Father who [is] in the heavens.

12.w: What do you⁺ think? If unto any man there should be a hundred sheep, and one of them should go astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and, having gone, seek the one going astray?

13.w: And if it should come to pass [that] he finds it, truly I say to you⁺ that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine not having gone astray.

14.w: Thus it is not the will of your⁺ Father who [is] in the heavens that one of these little ones should be lost.

15.w: And if your brother may sin against you, go reprove him between you and him alone. If he may hear you, you have gained your brother.

16.w: But if he may not hear, take with you one or two more, so that ‘every word may be stood upon the testimony of two or three witnesses.’

17.w: And if he may fail to hear them, say [it] to the church. And if he may fail to hear even the church, let him be unto you as the Gentile and the tax collector.

18.w: Truly I say to you⁺, whatever you⁺ shall bind on the earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you⁺ shall loose on the earth will be loosed in heaven.

19.w: Again, truly I say to you⁺ that if two of you⁺ on the earth shall agree about any matter that they shall ask, it will be done for them by My Father who [is] in the heavens.

20.w: For where two or three are gathered together unto My name, there am I in their midst.”

21.w: Then, having come, Peter said to Him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me, and I will forgive him? Up to seven times?”

22.w: Jesus says to him, “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times!

23.w: Because of this, the kingdom of the heavens was likened to to a man, a king, who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

24.w: And [on] his having begun to settle, one was brought to him, a debtor of ten thousand talents.

25.w: And [on] his having nothing to repay, the master commanded him to be sold—and the wife and the children and all of whatever he had—and repayment to be made.

26.w: Therefore the servant, having fallen down, was bowing on his knees to him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay all to you.’

27.w: And having been moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt.

28.w: But having gone out, that servant found one of his fellow servants who was owing him a hundred denarii. And having seized him, he was choking [him], saying, ‘Repay what you owe!’

29.w: Therefore, having fallen down, his fellow servant was calling on him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’

30.w: But he was not willing. Rather, having gone, he cast him into prison until he should repay what was owed.

31.w: Therefore his fellow servants, having seen the things having happened, were deeply grieved, and having gone, they made clear to their master all the things having happened.

32.w: Then, having summoned him, his master says to him, ‘Evil servant! I forgave you all that debt because you called on me.

33.w: Was it not necessary for you also to have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I also had mercy on you?’

34.w: And having become angry, his master delivered him to the tormenters until he should repay everything being owed to him.

35.w: Thus also My heavenly Father will do to you⁺ unless each of you⁺ should forgive his brother from your⁺ hearts.”
